anomalies.observed: The netlist and SPICE deck show all six 0 Ω jumpers populated: R1 and R23 both connect /NET0039 to J1/J8 pin 19 and pin 21; R5 and R14 both connect /NET0003 to J1/J8 pin 22 and pin 20; R8 and R21 connect Net-(J6-Pin_3), Net-(J11-Pin_3), and U2 pin 6 (/NET0031). With R2 and R20 present, the PWM GPIO nets are also tied through 1 kΩ resistors to the MAX3485 serial bus.
anomalies.expected: The design is intended to be in one mutually exclusive mode: PWM mode with only the appropriate one PWM selection jumper per channel populated and serial bridge jumpers open, or serial mode with only the serial bridge jumpers populated and PWM selection jumpers open. Pin 19/21 and pin 20/22 must not be shorted together.

evidence.quote: two mutually-exclusive servo interface modes, selected at assembly time by populating different 0 Ω jumper resistors
R9–R12 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | Select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2
R13, R14 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | When shorted, bridge J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 together and onto the MAX3485 TTL bus — schematic note: "Short R13, R14 for Serial Servo"

anomalies.impact: This creates a hybrid PWM/serial connection not supported by the intended design. It shorts two alternative M5Stack GPIO pins together for each channel, causing GPIO contention, possible damage, and loss of independent PWM control; it also loads the MAX3485 serial bus through the 1 kΩ PWM resistors, potentially corrupting serial servo communication.

parsed.summary: The board contains an anomaly because the design files show all PWM selection jumpers and all serial bridge jumpers populated, violating the mutually exclusive PWM/serial mode selection and shorting M5Stack bus GPIO pins.
